title: Kiipsaare Lighthouse
visualBrief: Slender slightly leaning weathered concrete lighthouse with narrow recessed openings, worn paint courses, exposed threshold, circular gallery, empty lantern frame and rust-colored shallow cupola.

sourceFacts.currentSetting: In the sea on unstable ground; angle of inclination changes.
sourceFacts.basis: Estonian national tourism agency description and official project photographs. Cached Wikidata25m differs from the primary tourism26m; primary26m used.

referenceRights: VisitEstonia photographs consulted as primary location references; images are not embedded, copied as textures or redistributed.

nativeAxes.origin: Approximate visible base/waterline reference; photographic2-degree lean toward-X is baked into this static source.

geographicProposal.notes: Photographer GPS and a front-facing door give a reconstructed northwest quadrant only, +/-20 degrees; the exact entrance bearing is not surveyed. The tower lean changes, and -2 degrees is a static representative pose. No tower footprint, submerged footing, bathymetry, current tide or accurate shore outline is claimed. Society 21.8213066 longitude contradicts the national tourism and exact-QID positions and is excluded. +Y up; +Z faces the reconstructed northwest entry/viewpoint direction. Baked representative -2-degree local X lean therefore points northeast; this is not a measured present tilt. National tourism and inspected photographs show the visible base in the sea. Source Y=0 represents the model waterline placed at the host sea-level plane. It is a visual datum convention, not a measured tide or submerged footing height.

limitations: Original exterior reconstruction from documented main dimensions and inspected references. Individual moldings, sections, weathering, openings and fittings are photo-proportioned estimates.
No interior visitor route, surveyed collision model, operating navigation-light simulation or exact optical assembly is included. Lantern glazing is a restrained opaque PBR approximation.
Shared material references use metric UVs with portable vertex-color PBR fallback. Maximum-fidelity, lit shared-surface and geographic fit reviews remain separate pending gates.

The2-degree lean is a representative photo-proportioned pose, not a current survey; the authority says it varies. Diameter, gallery, lantern framing and irregular paint bands are photo estimates. Water level, seabed/submerged footing and door azimuth remain unresolved. No intact lens or active beacon is invented.

appearance.identity: Slender abandoned tapered concrete lighthouse with surviving cream bands, three narrow stair windows, open lantern frame and rusted shallow cupola.
appearance.epoch: Weathered abandoned exterior in the inspected national tourism photos and credited September 2023 base photograph; no operating lens or glass is invented.
appearance.master: Retain original 13632-triangle master and representative two-degree lean byte-for-byte.
appearance.browser: Authored far levels retain paint ranks, taper, lean, gallery and open lantern. District keeps actual recessed apertures, reduces regular radial subdivisions and repeated rail fittings. Original detailed source supplies street and closeup.
appearance.exclusions: Precise current lean, surveyed azimuth or fine dimensions, operational optics, tide, bathymetry, submerged foundation and exact present shore geometry.
